extracted.intended_audience: web managers and content strategists (digital teams, public-sector content creators)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for creating public-facing web content that is clear, easy to understand, and compliant with the Plain Writing Act; aimed at helping digital teams design, write, and test content for specific audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plain language – content that is clear and easy to understand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plain language is critical to helping the public make sense of their obligations and benefits. Not only is plain language more efficient and effective, it is also the law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Write for your specific audience
rubrics_metrics.description: The Plain Writing Act of 2010 established the requirement that content for the public is written for its specific audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content should be created, designed, and tested so that the specific audience understands it; the guides are designed to help web managers and content strategists apply audience-focused practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of plain language
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of plain language principles, writing for your audience, and the Plain Writing Act of 2010.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the principles guide to learn foundational criteria (such as clarity, organization, tone, and audience focus) that underpin effective plain-language content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing for understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Overview of how to write clear content that follows plain language guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on writing techniques that promote comprehension (word choice, sentence structure, organization) so readers can understand information and act on it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design for understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: How content design can support plain language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use content design (layout, headings, visual hierarchy, formatting) to make information scannable and usable, thereby supporting plain-language goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test for understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn how to test that your content is easily understandable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply user testing and evaluation to verify that intended audiences can understand and use the content; testing closes the loop between creation and effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law and policy compliance (Plain Writing Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plain language is a legal requirement for public-facing government content under the Plain Writing Act of 2010.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure content practices and governance meet the Act's requirement that public-facing communications be written for their specific audiences; incorporate compliance into workflows and training.
